A mortgage enabling first-time buyers to get on the housing ladder with a deposit as low as 2% has been launched by Leeds Building Society.

The Start Mortgage allows borrowers to access loans worth up to five times their income.

The deal requires a minimum deposit of £5,000, so people would need to be buying a home worth £250,000 or more for the deposit to be as low as 2%.

The maximum loan size is £500,000 and a minimum income of £30,000 is also required.

The mortgage, which is subject to affordability assessments, is available through brokers or direct with Leeds.

The society said that self-employed people can also apply and gift deposits are accepted – meaning the “bank of mum and dad” can potentially chip in.

The five-year product has a fixed rate of 5.65% with a free standard valuation and no fee payable on completion.

Some other lenders also offer low or no deposit mortgages to help first-time buyers.

Matt Bartle, director of mortgages at Leeds Building Society, said: “Saving for a deposit remains one of the biggest hurdles for first-time buyers.

“By reducing that barrier to just 2% and combining it with flexible lending criteria, we’re helping more people move closer to owning their own home.”

Rachel Springall, a finance expert at Moneyfacts, said: “The Start Mortgage is a rare 98% loan-to-value deal and as applicants can borrow up to five times their income, this launch could make a meaningful difference for would-be homeowners who might otherwise remain stuck in the rental cycle.”

News.title: Pound hits one-year high on hopes of Chancellor Mahmood
News.content:
The pound has hit a one-year high on hopes that Shabana Mahmood will be named Andy Burnham’s chancellor.

Sterling climbed 0.6pc against the euro to tip above €1.18, its highest level since June last year, after the Home Secretary emerged as the frontrunner to replace Rachel Reeves. Over the same timeframe, the pound rose as much as 0.8pc versus the dollar to more than $1.35.

Ms Mahmood is thought to be in pole position to take over from Rachel Reeves at the Treasury when Mr Burnham enters Downing Street on Monday, after weeks of speculation about his Cabinet choices.

Mr Miliband, the Energy Secretary, had previously been considered the top contender for No 11 after advising Mr Burnham, who won the Makerfield by-election last month, on his economic plans.

However, he is viewed less favourably by markets over concerns he will pursue a more Left-leaning agenda than rivals.

Philip Shaw, chief UK economist at Investec, said the pound had performed strongly against the euro and dollar as reports that Ms Mahmood was the frontrunner to become the next Chancellor were “soothing market fears of unduly lax fiscal policy”.

The rally for the pound also came as Britain’s economy returned to growth in May in a boost for incoming prime minister Andy Burnham.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.1pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

It marked a rebound from a 0.1pc decline in April, which had been the first contraction in eight months.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics said the economy has been “more resilient” than previously thought but warned higher fuel prices would still restrain real incomes.

He said the 0.1pc rise in UK GDP in May “is not a bad welcome gift for incoming prime minister Andy Burnham”.

News.title: At the moment of reckoning, England’s old anxiety took hold
News.content:
All the years that have passed since those red shirts on a summer’s day at a long-gone Wembley Stadium – the humiliations, the occasional triumph, the plentiful servings of self-pity. For a short while in Atlanta it felt like that epoch might finally be ending and all it came down to was managing the last five minutes and whatever the beleaguered referee might add.

A place at a World Cup final was within England’s grasp, a mere 60 years since the last. But just as it loomed into view, already the players and their manager were tracing an old path. The man currently in charge of the England team might be German, the players might be of a generation finessed under bold new coaching ideas, but once more a familiar anxiety took hold. England were minutes from the prize. Yet team and manager were already obeying an old instinct to sabotage the moment.

England had been in retreat long before Lionel Messi served up for Enzo Fernández the goal that would level this World Cup semi-final, and then the second for Lautaro Martínez ,which would propel Argentina forward. Of course, Messi is Messi, and this Argentina team exist to exert his will on games by any means necessary. Yet, as ever, at the moment of reckoning, England demonstrated all the resistance of damp cardboard.

Thomas Tuchel once again reverted to the deep defensive position. Once again, the adapted five-man back line sat on the edge of their area. Against Mexico in the last 16, Tuchel was dismissive of any suggestion he had invited pressure, asking what other option he had with just 10 men. Against Norway in the quarter-finals he did the same, once Erling Haaland was off the pitch. Against Argentina, a team accustomed to playing with it all on the line, such a move was fatal.

News.title: Dengue outbreak complicates Bangladesh measles crisis response
News.content:
A major outbreak of dengue fever threatens to overwhelm hospitals in Bangladesh, where an explosive measles epidemic has already pushed the health system to the brink.

From the start of the year to the end of May, Bangladesh recorded 714 dengue cases and 1 death. By July 6, that had soared to 7,110 cases and 19 deaths.

Meanwhile more than 113,000 people have required hospital treatment for measles, with 718 of them dying, the vast majority among children under five.

Experts warn the dual crisis is putting more lives at risk.

“If you have a dengue outbreak that is already going to stretch public healthcare resources, and on top of that you have measles, this could become a huge burden, both on the resources and on the doctors and healthcare workers managing the patients,” Dr Ooi Eng Eong, a dengue expert and head of the Environmental Health Institute, National Environment Agency in Singapore, told The Telegraph.

Two diseases share enough symptoms to be mistaken for one another, with potentially fatal consequences.

“They present in a similar way, with fever and rash. It’s well documented that, in the past, measles cases have been mistaken for dengue, and dengue has been misdiagnosed as measles,” said Dr Eng Eong.

“Unfortunately, the treatment, especially to prevent progression to severe dengue, is quite different from how you would treat a measles case. So misdiagnosis could have quite important consequences for patients.”

News.title: Spain deliver footballing lesson to send France packing
News.content:
Whether you use your eyes or the underlying data, France and Spain look like the two best teams at this World Cup but only one of them will play in Sunday’s final in New Jersey.

France are the tournament’s top goalscorers with 16 goals in six matches, while European champions Spain have the best defence.

France have certainly played as a team at this tournament, but their great strength is a luxurious level of individual quality across a front four of Desire Doue, Michael Olise, Ousmane Dembele and Kylian Mbappe. Spain rely more on their collective patterns of play and a distinctive style which is very much their own.

Most opponents at this World Cup have sat off France and hoped to limit the damage, but Spain will not approach the game in that way which should make this an absorbing contest. Spain will want to hide the ball from France’s best players and ask questions of a defence which has been relatively untroubled.

However, the more possession Spain have, the higher up the pitch their centre-backs Aymeric Laporte and Pau Curbasi will be, which could leave them vulnerable to a fleet-footed France attack in transition.

If Spain are to hurt France, Lamine Yamal against either Theo Hernandez or Lucas Digne looks the most likely avenue. Left-back is the one position in France’s team in which they do not have an elite option.

Spain have been utterly dominant for long stretches of their matches, but have not converted that control into goals in the manner of France, and that could well be the difference. Mbappe is currently the tournament’s joint top scorer on eight goals, level with Lionel Messi and one behind Argentine in the all-time list of World Cup top scorers.

Messi, and England, will be watching this closely and it ought to be a cracker in Dallas.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Brainless batting seals England’s fate as India win first ODI
News.content:
It was a sporting wicket and England did not help themselves by picking the wrong side. They were a spinner too heavy and a seamer light. India could just motor through the middle overs once they averted losing wickets when the ball was hard, their only wobble was when Shubman Gill retired hurt for 80 but Washington Sundar and Axar Patel are old lags and saw India home with 28 balls to spare.

Edgbaston was full and gave the Blue for Bob charity a good send-off. This was the last money-raising day for prostate cancer in memory of Bob Willis after seven years raising £2m for prostate cancer research. Willis would have relished laying into some of England’s batting.

It is more than a decade since England relaunched their 50-over cricket at Edgbaston, scoring 408 against McCullum’s New Zealand and setting themselves on the path to World Cup glory. Then they were full of zest and new ideas. Something they have never replicated.

There are three survivors from that side still going. Of that trio, Root remains the most valuable and consistent. This innings took his career average over 50 and since making a hundred at the Champions Trophy last year he has averaged 70.

Jos Buttler scored a 77-ball 129 in that New Zealand game in 2015 and was a World Cup final hero four years later. This was his 200th ODI and Eoin Morgan presented him with a commemorative cap before play. Buttler’s 131 off 64 balls in the final T20 on Saturday was a reminder of what he can still do after a lean run but there are no guarantees he makes it to the World Cup in the same way that Root appears a rock-solid bet.

Buttler made five here and with other candidates to bat and keep, there might be a call for McCullum to make at some point down the line. Adil Rashid was the other survivor from that NZ ODI. He will be 39 at the next World Cup and you wonder if England may regret not giving Rehan Ahmed more experience. Rashid was milked, which generally happens when he plays India.

In 26-year-old Gurnoor Brar, India have found another strapping, punchy fast bowler who likes a battle, and after a wobbly start he struck twice in the 13th over – Jacob Bethell for a sticky 14 from 31, and Ben Duckett after a jaunty 43. Gill brought back Bumrah, he knocked over Brook with his first ball. Prasidh Krishna’s double-wicket maiden – Buttler caught off a leading edge and Sam Curran nicking behind – left England 80 for five.

News.title: Interest rates to ‘rise by September’ as oil prices surge
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Oil prices surged to the highest level in a month after the US launched a third night of strikes on Iran.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to more than $85 a barrel as Donald Trump also reimposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

Oil prices had leapt nearly 10pc on Monday as the ceasefire in the Middle East was left in tatters and the US president said America would charge a toll for protecting the Strait of Hormuz.

The US military launched five-hours of strikes which sought to “degrade Iran’s ability to attack commercial shipping”.

The United Arab Emirates said Iran struck two ships in the strait overnight, killing one crew member.

Mr Trump said Monday that the United States was “taking over” the waterway, where a fifth of the world’s oil and gas exports pass during peacetime.

He said the US would slap a toll of 20pc on all cargo shipped through the strait, in an announcement that drew mockery from Iran and accusations of “piracy” from critics.

Mr Trump said a deal with Tehran was still possible even as attacks were carried out. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Reeves calls for ‘stability’ in last-ditch attempt to remain Chancellor | Mansion House speech will argue Labour has made ‘huge strides’ in repairing economy

2) I know how the Treasury works. These are the taxes Burnham will target | Landlords, big business, banks and the wealthy will be asked to fund measures to ease the cost of living

3) Chris Packham pressures Burberry to drop cashmere | Presenter criticises British luxury fashion brand for using ‘inherently violent’ production method

4) Rhine drought cripples shipping in blow to Germany | Factories depend on river to transport up to 200 million tonnes of goods and fuel each year

5) Paramount accused of ‘blackmail’ with threat to leave Hollywood | States file lawsuit challenging Hollywood studio giant’s takeover of Warner Bros

What happened overnight

Oil prices climbed as fighting intensified in the Middle East.

The price of Brent crude climbed to just over $84 a barrel after soaring nearly 10pc on Monday. US benchmark crude was up 1.4pc at $79.20 a barrel.

Oil prices are still below their wartime peak of more than $126 a barrel, but uncertainty over the future stability of supplies deepened as the US and Iran each asserted they controlled the Strait of Hormuz.

The US launched more strikes on Iran overnight after Donald Trump said Washington was “reinstating” a blockade on Iran in the strait.

Fighting in the region has kept oil tankers from using the waterway to deliver crude to customers from the Persian Gulf, driving up fuel prices worldwide.

Meanwhile Asian shares declined, dragged lower by losses for artificial-intelligence stocks.

In Asian trading, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 lost 1pcto 66,574.96 and the Kospi in South Korea declined 3.2pc to 6,589.37.

The Shanghai Composite index lost 0.8oc to 3,884.32, even though the government reported that China’s exports jumped 27pc in June from a year earlier as adoption of artificial intelligence drove strong demand for computer chips and other technology.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged 0.1pc higher, to 24,230.46, while in Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 shed 0.5pc to 8,767.00.

On Monday on Wall Street, the S&P 500 fell 0.8pc, coming off its fourth winning week in the last five. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3pc, and the Nasdaq Composite sank 1.6pc.

News.title: Ebola outbreak threatens to halt pioneering UK-backed kidney transplant programme
News.content:
The Ebola outbreak could halt a pioneering UK-backed kidney transplant programme that made the operation available in Uganda for the first time.

A team of surgeons from Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is due to travel to Kampala in August but may be forced to cancel if the outbreak is still active, doctors at Mulago National Referral Hospital, where the programme is based, told The Telegraph.

At least 20 people have been infected with Bundibugyo Ebola, a rare species of the virus for which there is no approved vaccine, in Uganda. All of them have been isolated at Mulago Hospital, on the same campus as the transplant unit.

Although there have not been any new cases in Uganda for more than three weeks, an outbreak can only be considered over once 42 days have passed, according to World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines.

The kidney transplant initiative, launched in 2023, is delivered through SCALE, a partnership between the NHS and Ugandan health authorities.

British surgeons regularly travel to Uganda for intensive two-week surgical “camps” held four times a year, during which they perform transplants alongside local teams while training them to eventually run the service independently.

The August camp is expected to carry out between 10 and 15 kidney transplants from living donors.

If it is postponed, some patients could be forced to drop out of the process over expensive preparation costs.

Sports.title: Britain dismisses Argie rage over UK warship’s ‘innocent passage’ near Falklands as protest lodged after World Cup clash
Sports.content:
BRITAIN has dismissed Argentinian protests over a Royal Navy warship sailing through its waters near the Falkland Islands.

Buenos Aires lodged a furious complaint after HMS Medway, an offshore patrol ship, sailed to and from the Antarctic.



London insisted the voyage complied with maritime law and the Argentinian government was warned long in advance.

The warship was making an “innocent passage” which is guaranteed under the Law of the Sea, the Navy said.



It is the same reason Russian warships are free to transit the Channel and British and US vessels sail through the Taiwan strait, despite protests from China.

Hours after Argentina dumped England out of the World Cup with a dramatic 2-1 semi-final win, Buenos Aires said the Medway went on an “unconsulted and illegal” passage.



Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno claimed the warship illegally entered Argentine waters earlier this month without prior warning.

Britain’s Ministry of Defence quickly dismissed the Argie protest.

An MoD spokesperson said: “HMS Medway undertook a routine logistics visit to Punta Arenas on 5-8 July supporting British Antarctic Survey operations, delivering essential stores and supplies to sustain scientific research in Antarctica.

“The transit from the Falkland Islands to Chile and back was carried out via the most direct practicable route, considering operational safety and weather factors to ensure timely delivery.”



A No 10 spokeswoman added: “The Royal Navy always operates in full compliance with international law.”

Defence insiders said the voyage was conducted in accordance with Article 17 of the United Nations Convention on the Laws of the Sea.

HMS Medway, a Batch 2 River-class offshore patrol vessel, has been based in the Falklands since January.



It replaced HMS Forth as the Royal Navy’s permanent guard ship in the territorial waters.

The flashpoint comes as Reform boss Nigel Farage urged Downing Street to focus on building up the Royal Navy.

He said: “Whilst I am disgusted at the behaviour of some Argentinian players last night, the most important thing to do is build up the Royal Navy quickly.”

English and Argentine relations have come under serious scrutiny this week both before and after the World Cup clash.

Ahead of the game, Argentina’s hate-filled vice-president branded England “usurping pirates” over the Falklands.



President Javier Milei brazenly also cheered his government’s shameless push to snatch the Falklands back from Britain.

Britain has had control of the islands since winning a bitter war to defend them from Buenos Aires in 1982, who invaded and occupied the territory.

The conflict claimed the lives of 255 UK servicemen, three islanders, and 649 Argentine personnel.



After winning Wednesday night’s match, Argentina’s players held up a sign reading “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” which translates in English to The Falklands are Argentine.

This has caused uproar at home with Downing Street now backing calls for Fifa to probe whether Argentina players broke rules after flaunting the political banner.

A statement from No10 on the controversy said: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch also pledged that the Conservatives would always fight to defend the Falklands Islands.

She said: “The Falkland Islands are British. The Conservatives will always defend them.”



Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey echoed these calls while saying he has penned a letter to Fifa asking them to suspend the players who held up the controversial banner.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He took to social media to say: “In August 2024 Rodri and Álvaro Morata were rightly banned for one match for singing ‘Gibraltar is Spain.’

“Now the Argentine players who celebrated with the ‘Falklands are Argentine’ banner must be barred from the final.”

Sports.title: Horrifying World Cup semi-final stat makes miserable reading for England after Argentina defeat
Sports.content:
ENGLAND failed to advance to the World Cup final after a harrowing 2-1 defeat to Argentina.

Anthony Gordon‘s opener lifted the hopes of the nation but the tragic ending revealed a terrifying statistic about English football.



Gordon tucked the ball into the corner past Emi Martinez in the 56th minute.

Then for 30 minutes, it looked as if he may become the unlikely hero needed to carry England through.



But the one-way traffic from Argentina and the relentless press in a low block ultimately earned Enzo Fernandez the equaliser.

All the Three Lions needed to do was hold out for extra time and their World Cup dreams could regroup.



But Lautaro Martinez struck in injury time to send the South Americans into the final.

There have only been two times this century that a team has scored first in a men’s World Cup semi final and still failed to reach the final.

And BOTH were England.

In 2018, the Three Lions made their first appearance in a World Cup semi final since Italia ’90.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Kieran Trippier – another former Newcastle man – handed England the perfect start with a 20-yard free-kick after only five minutes.

But Ivan Perisic‘s equaliser in the 68th minute sent the match into extra time.

And then Mario Mandzukic scored the winning goal in the 109th minute.



This sent Croatia into their first ever World Cup final against France, who won 4-2.

England will have to wait another four years for a shot at redemption when the World Cup is set to be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal, and Morocco.

Before that they will have a shot at a home Euros with it due to be held between England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland.

In the meantime, England will face France on Saturday in a bid to secure third-place, which would still be their second best finish.

Meanwhile, Argentina will advance to play Spain on Sunday as they look to win back-to-back World Cup titles.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: William Saliba facing major injury worry, Leandro Trossard bags big contract and new documentary launched
Sports.content:
WILLIAM SALIBA is expected to play no part when France face England this weekend, amid fears he requires back surgery.

The Arsenal defender was forced off during the first-half of Les Blues’ defeat to Spain in the World Cup semi-finals on Tuesday night.

Saliba was complaining of back pain, which he’s been managing during the tournament and he is due to undergo further tests.



The centre-back is expected to be left out of the squad when France take on England in Miami on Saturday in the third-place play-off.



Crystal Palace centre-back Maxence Lacroix is the most likely to come into the side after replacing Saliba on Tuesday night.

Surgery has been floated as a possibility for the Arsenal defender this summer – but a final decision has not been made yet.

Saliba being absent for an extended spell would be a hammer blow to Arsenal, who are already sweating on the fitness of Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice.



The England stars have not looked fully fit at the World Cup and Saka was an unused substitute during Wednesday’s semi-final loss to Argentina.

Rice was forced off after 82 minutes of the 2-1 loss and has been digging deep in the US to feature for England after a long season with Arsenal.

Saliba last suffered a back injury three years ago in March 2023 and it forced him to miss the rest of that season.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

A long lay-off now may force Arsenal to rethink their transfer plans, although they have already been targeting a new defender this summer.



Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa has been mooted as a target and would provide cover in both the heart of defence and at right-back.

Saliba being injured could also impact Arsenal’s outgoings, with Ben White touted as a possible departure.

The right-back can also play in the middle of defence and could fill in for Saliba if needed.

White first joined Arsenal as a centre-back, arriving from Brighton for £50million in 2021, and formed a good partnership with Gabriel.

TAKE IT TO THE MAX

MAX DOWMAN’S match-worn merchandise is going for bigger sums than all of his Arsenal team-mates.



The teenager burst onto the scene last season and became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history.

Dowman, 16, was also on the bench for the Champions League final and is expected to have an increased role in the upcoming campaign.

The winger’s popularity has been made clear by how well his worn training kit is selling for in online auctions.

The website MatchWornShirts held an auction for Arsenal’s pre-match Champions League warm-up shirts from last season.

And Dowman’s went for more than any other Gunners player, eventually being sold for £988. The next highest seller was Declan Rice’s pre-match top, which was snapped up for £762.



That was an auction for the short sleeve warm-up shirt, but Dowman also topped the sale for the long-sleeve version.

Dowman’s one in that category went for £664 and Rice, again, was second with his going for £481.

A training wear bundle from Premier League games also had Dowman as the biggest seller among Arsenal players, with that set being sold for £1,487.

For context, captain Martin Odegaard’s worn bundle was auctioned off for £566.



MIK’S EMOTIONS

ARSENAL’S World Cup stars have shone across the pond this summer – racking up 22 goal contributions at the tournament.

That tally means only Real Madrid have had more influence on the tournament than the Gunners.

Arsenal’s representatives have managed nine goals and 13 assists at the tournament and could still add to that with three stars in Spain’s squad for Sunday’s final.

David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are all available for Luis de la Fuente’s side.



As impressive as Arsenal’s contribution to the tournament has been, it could be to the detriment of their pre-season preparations.

Arsenal had 15 players picked to represent their country, and every one of them advanced out of the group stages.

Mikel Arteta is set to give an extended break to the players who participated in the World Cup.

A host of Arsenal aces who did not travel to the World Cup are currently taking part in a Marbella training camp.

WORTH THE WAIT

ARSENAL were crowned Premier League champions nearly two months ago – but the demand for club merchandise is not slowing down.



After winning the title, the Gunners released their new home shirt for next season with ‘Champions’ and the number 26 on the back of it.

The shirt is on sale for £113 via the official club store online and it has proved incredibly popular.

Indeed, fans logging onto the website this week found that it is not in stock – unless you want it in an extra small size.

The other sizes are all out of stock and supporters can ask to be notified when they are available again.

Even the kids version of the shirt – which costs £88 – is in limited supply and is out of stock in several sizes.



HOUR OF NEED

ARSENAL have launched a THREE-HOUR documentary recounting their title-winning campaign.

Fans who want to relive the highs and lows of a historic campaign can enjoy the Season Review show on the Arsenal app.

The Gunners have already ensured fans can revel in every moment of their title success.



They previously launched a 24/7 live stream showing footage from the title celebrations, as well as a three-and-a-half hour replay of their trophy parade.

A documentary about Merino’s journey to return from injury was also released on the app in recent weeks.

TURKISH DELIGHT

LEANDRO TROSSARD has finally joined Besiktas after the Turkish club spent a year chasing his signature.

Besiktas had in fact been pushing to sign the Belgian last summer, but he stayed at Arsenal and landed a pay rise.

They returned this summer, though, and the Gunners agreed to sell as Trossard was into the final year of his contract.



Besiktas, unlike many other clubs, have also revealed the full terms of the transfer after announcing it on Wednesday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Turkish side are paying €18million (£15.3m) upfront and that will be paid in six equal installments over three years.

Trossard’s contract is for three years, with the option to extend it by a further 12 months, and is worth a guaranteed sum of £105,000-a-week.

Sports.title: How Thomas Tuchel’s substitutions compare to Gareth Southgate’s in big matches – which England boss is more defensive?
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL’s substitutions in England’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina quickly drew comparisons with Gareth Southgate.

The former England boss was harshly treated for his pragmatic approach to knockout football, with England making a number of deep cup runs under his stewardship, but wilting against the biggest opponents.



Fans naturally drew parallels to the memory of Southgate’s England when Tuchel decided to introduce THREE defenders off the bench against Argentina in a desperate bid to hold on to the narrow lead provided by Anthony Gordon‘s opener.

But a closer examination shows that even Southgate never dared to throw his side quite so far into reverse gear in a match of such magnitude.



Goalscorer Gordon was hooked for central defender Ezri Konsa in the 72nd minute, with England already on the back foot, having retreated to their own defensive third since taking the lead.

After a flurry of chances for the South American side, Tuchel doubled down on his new approach, adding towering defenders Dan Burn and Nico O’Reilly to the mix at the expense of the more technically gifted Declan Rice and Reece James.



Those moves ceded even more possession to Argentina, with England holding on to the ball for just 12 PER CENT of the match between their opener and Enzo Fernandez’s inevitable equaliser.

Lautaro Martinez had already added a second by the time Tuchel decided to U-turn again and bring on Ivan Toney and Marcus Rashford to try and rescue his side’s botched last stand.

Compare that flurry of defensive substitutions to Southgate’s last game in charge, England’s Euro 2024 final loss to Spain.

England went down to the Spaniards in the 47th minute, with Southgate seeing out another quarter of an hour before making his first change, bringing Ollie Watkins on in place of Harry Kane – a tactic that had worked just days earlier when Watkins’ late winner off the bench sank the Netherlands in the semis.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

He then shook things up again in his attack, bringing Cole Palmer on for Kobbie Mainoo, who promptly equalised for England three minutes later.

Mikel Oyarzabal struck back for Spain, prompting Southgate to throw Toney on with minutes left in the match in the vain hope of finding some late magic.

The match ended with three England subs, all of which saw an attacker enter the field.

But that match started with England fighting an uphill battle – a better analogy of Wednesday’s clash would be the Euros final against Italy in 2021, in which England took a lead within minutes of the match starting which they failed to defend.

Southgate did not make any subs until after Leonardo Bonucci‘s equaliser, before introducing Bukayo Saka in place of Kieran Trippier minutes later.



He then swapped Jordan Henderson on for Rice in normal time, before adding Jack Grealish into the mix early in extra time.

England failed to hold on to a narrow lead and Italy punished them on penalties, drawing comparisons to Tuchel’s performance – but his predecessor did not exactly throw the brakes on with a series of defensive substitutions.

In fact, Tuchel had form for the approach even before the semis, with substitutions like bringing Burn on for Elliot Anderson against Mexico and bringing Reece James on for Gordon against Norway.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Though it wasn’t always all-out defence when the German tactician turned to his reinforcements, there was a clear thread of leaning on a beefed-up back line when enjoying leads in big games, something that Southgate rarely turned to against top opposition.

With all this in mind, it’s harsh to compare Wednesday’s capitulation to Southgate’s record in big games, even if his approach was already agonisingly cautious at times.

Sports.title: ‘Should have carried on pushing’ – Marc Guehi calls out Thomas Tuchel’s England tactics in World Cup exit to Argentina
Sports.content:
MARC GUEHI claims that England shouldn’t have played so defensively after taking the lead against Argentina.

The Three Lions exited the World Cup at the semi-final stage after losing 2-1 to their old rivals in Atlanta.



Anthony Gordon prodded England into the lead on 55 minutes, only for late goals by Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez to turn the contest on its head.

Thomas Tuchel‘s side had just 12 per cent possession between Gordon’s opener and Martinez’s 92nd minute winner.



The Three Lions boss moved to a 5-4-1 formation in that time, throwing on Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O’Reilly.

Plenty of pundits, including the likes of Wayne Rooney, Joe Hart, Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, have criticised Tuchel’s tactical decisions.

And Guehi has suggested that he did not agree either.

The Manchester City defender, 26, said: “Once we went 1-0 up we seemed to just try and hold on, which at this level is just not enough, so I’m gutted.”

Guehi went on to add: “We should have carried on. We should have carried on pushing.

“It kind of felt like we scored and then the mentality was go back, defend.”



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

On if this England group is capable of finally getting over the line at a future tournament, glum Guehi said: “I don’t know. I don’t know. It’s hard to think about the future right now.

“At this moment, it’s just disappointment. That’s all.”

On Tuchel’s second half changes, BBC pundit Rooney said: “We got ourselves in such a good position and we didn’t know what to do.

“We sat back, allowed them to come on to us. They put us under pressure and we cracked. As soon as they got the first goal, it was inevitable they’d get the second.

“When you go on top, you have to stay on top. We go 1-0 up, then sit back, make changes, go five or six at the back. If you allow (Lionel) Messi and Argentina to come onto you, you’re asking for trouble.”



In February Tuchel, 52, signed a two-year contract extension up to Euro 2028.

Despite criticism, the German said after last night’s game: “We keep on going with the contract until the home Euros.

“I’m looking forward to that even though right now it’s difficult to look that far ahead.

“A lot of big football nations are eliminated before the semi-final, so it is an achievement.

“No-one wants to hear that at the moment; me neither because we demand the most of ourselves. That’s just the nature of being competitive.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tuchel is said to retain the full backing of the FA.

The former Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain boss has won 16 of his 21 games in charge, drawing two and losing three.

Sports.title: England LIVE REACTION: Falkands row, Tuchel future latest after Argentina heartbreak
Sports.content:
Argentina stars fuelled by history and politics

By Ryan Taylor in Atlanta, Georgia.

Lionel Messi, Lisandro Martinez and Leandro Paredes have all admitted they used history and political tensions to find an extra gear to beat England.

The World Cup holders posed with a flag that read, 'The Falklands are Argentinian' after they came from behind to eliminate the Three Lions and reach Sunday's final where they will face Spain.

After providing two assists for Enzo Fernandez and sub Lautaro Martinez, Messi revealed that he used the raw fan emotion - due the past - to drag La Albiceleste over the line: "Everything we experienced was incredible, from the very beginning, as we said.

"Although it was a football match, when we started to enter the field and during the anthem, we experienced special feelings, and the group felt that. It wasn't just another victory; it was an important victory that the Argentine people wanted, and we wanted it too, and it put us in another World Cup final." Manchester United defender Martinez also felt similarly, explaining: “I won’t lie to you, we’re all Argentinians and we experienced it like the fans. We knew the magnitude of this game and went for it from the first minute.

"We had to suffer because they’re a very tough opponent, but in the end, we’re always the ones who take the initiative, the ones who play without fear, and the ones who want to win."

Meanwhile, Paredes appeared to pay tribute to those that lost their lives in the Falklands war, stating: “We are aware of what England means to this country, to us, and to history, because of that sad moment the people experienced and who are surely very happy today."

England led on 55 minutes through Anthony Gordon before dropping deep and trying to protect their 1-0 lead. Unfortunately for Thomas Tuchel his defensive changes did not pay dividends and only enabled Messi to work his magic as he first teed up Fernandez for a stunner before crossing for Inter Milan frontman Martinez.

He continued, revelling in Argentina's glory: "This group doesn't surprise me. I know and we know what we were capable of.

"People had doubts about how we arrived because we had players who were very much at their limit and with problems, but when this group comes together and is united, it always gives an extra boost, they inspire each other and bring out what they didn't have to give their all."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel told FIVE 'facts' about England vs Argentina as his decisions are ripped apart
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel told FIVE 'facts' about England vs Argentina as his decisions are ripped apart

Former Premier League boss Alan Pardew slammed Thomas Tuchel's decisions for England against Argentina

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has been criticised by Alan Pardew (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Former Premier League boss Alan Pardew has unleashed a withering breakdown of where England manager Thomas Tuchel went wrong against Argentina. The Three Lions suffered a painful 2-1 semi-final defeat after surrendering a second-half lead.

‌



England opened the scoring through Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute, but a succession of defensive substitutions gifted the initiative to Argentina. Enzo Fernandez levelled the match with five minutes remaining before Lautaro Martinez clinched the win for the defending champions in added time.

‌



Pardew has managed 318 Premier League games across five clubs, notably coaching Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni during his time at West Ham United. The 64-year-old utilised his experience to deliver what he labelled an "FA report" on England's performance.

‌



The former Newcastle United and Crystal Palace boss pulled no punches in his assessment of Tuchel's errors on Wednesday night, which cost England a place in the World Cup final. During an appearance on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs show, Pardew broke his verdict down into "five facts".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Pardew's first point was a relatively encouraging one, as he claimed Tuchel had set up his team to play "positive" football. He believed that the three changes made to bring Morgan Rodgers, Djed Spence and John Stones were "justified".

‌



"Argentina looked rattled and overhyped," Pardew said. "The referee was poor and was so lenient with continuous fouling. The first half was intriguing, actually, and Anderson around Messi had worked, although disgracefully, he got the first booking.

"The second period, we remained the same up until we scored from a long Harry Kane pass into a vacant channel that I suggest was a tactical decision. Our reaction to that goal was poor. Argentina fuelled by a desire to push and work us over. " His remaining four points all centred on Thomas Tuchel's tactical shortcomings.

‌



Fact two: "Had Scaloni covered the faults made by Mexico and Norway when England had taken the lead? And the answer to that is emphatically, yes he would have. I worked with him. There's no way he wouldn't have gone over those facts.

View 3 Images Alan Pardew listed what he believed Tuchel got wrong against Argentina (Image: YouTube/@talkSPORT)

"They worked the backline by overloading the sides, now putting dipping crosses into our box and working shooting from the edge. Goalie and post saved us before breakthrough."

‌



Fact three: "72 minutes, three offensive changes by Argentina, which you would expect. We changed Konsa for Gordon. Right there was our biggest mistake. No offensive substitution at that time. Playing a semi-final, and we didn't use Saka, by the way, who was fit, to give us an outlet. So no tactical tweak to control possession and clear our box."

View 3 Images Lionel Scaloni (R) played under Pardew at West Ham (Image: Ben Radford/Getty Images)

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Fact four: "82 minutes, we changed Burn for James, O'Reilly for Rice. Rogers went to wing-back, O'Reilly to midfield. The team was now completely hamstrung as an offensive force."

Fact five: "Two players, Rogers and O'Reilly, playing positions never, ever played before. One as a wing-back and one as a tight man, three midfield. 85-minute goal, 93rd-minute winning goal. 96 minutes, Rashford and Toney, far too late.

In summary, he attributed the defeat to "fear, mistakes and the loss of rational organisation," further stating that "In truth, the manager fed a negative mindset."

"It's crazy to play two World Cup finals in a row. This group is incredible. Today we went looking for it again when things got tough, we never stopped believing, never stopped trying.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker jokes Thomas Tuchel is a 'Germany spy' with clear England agenda
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker jokes Thomas Tuchel is a 'Germany spy' with clear England agenda

Gary Lineker has made a lighthearted joke about Thomas Tuchel's England plan after the Three Lions were crashing out of the World Cup in the semi-finals

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has been blamed for England's World Cup exit (Image: Getty Images)

Gary Lineker has joked that Thomas Tuchel is a "German spy" whose job is to make sure England suffer because Germany are struggling so much at major tournaments.

‌



He is the first German to lead the Three Lions and had presided over a perfect qualification campaign and some impressive World Cup wins. His tactics and managerial IQ were seen as a difference maker, but England were undone by Argentina in the semi-finals.

‌



Tuchel is copping blame for the defeat with his defensive tactics, which had paid dividends against Mexico and Norway, proving the team's undoing. They invited huge amounts of pressure and Argentina eventually made it tell late in the game.

‌



Lineker has jokingly suggested that Germany have sent Tuchel in to ruin England's hopes of winning but did cast doubt over whether the ex-Chelsea boss should remain in his post.

Argentina fans burn England flag and carry coffin draped in Union Jack after World Cup win READ MORE :

The former England striker said on his Netflix show: “I just wonder whether Thomas Tuchel’s like a German spy, we’ve been infiltrated, I think Germany, because they’re not very good at the moment, they can’t get past the group stage, and I think they’ve sent in someone.

“I mean, I’m joking, I’m joking obviously, but he said after the Croatia game, he said, ‘if we lose, we’ll lose our way by playing aggressive, attacking football’, he went totally against that, didn’t he? I think the most frustrating thing as well was this team, they had a chance if they’d gone for it, and they just got it I think so wrong.

‌



“And is he the right man to take us forward? Well, I mean, I never ask for anyone to get sacked, I don’t think it’s the thing to do, but it depends on him and how he feels, and also how the FA feels.”

View 2 Images Germany have underwhelmed over the past decade in major tournaments (Image: Getty Images)

Germany have continued to underwhelm at major tournaments, enduring a steep decline since their World Cup win in 2014. They made the last four of the Euros in 2016 but since then have gone out at the group stages of two World Cups in 2018 and 2022, and were shocked by Paraguay in the Round of 32.

Article continues below

That cost Julian Nagelsmann his job and the Germans have now turned to Jurgen Klopp, who is tasked with taking the nation back to the summit of international football.

Sports.title: Mark Chapman sent home from World Cup as BBC star misses final round of matches
Sports.content:
Mark Chapman sent home from World Cup as BBC star misses final round of matches

Mark Chapman has another big job lined up after his World Cup stint

View 2 Images BBC presenter Mark Chapman is making a quick return to the UK (Image: BBC)

Mark Chapman has made a quick exit from the World Cup to be part of the BBC's coverage of the Open Championship. The Match of the Day host, who has been alternating presenting responsibilities with Gabby Logan, Kelly Cates and Alex Scott, led coverage of England's semi-final defeat to Argentina.

‌



He was joined by pundits Wayne Rooney, Joe Hart and Micah Richards in Atlanta. The BBC has only just decamped to the tournament en masse, having been based in their Salford studio for the majority of it.

‌



It's turned out to be an especially brief trip to America for the 52-year-old, who has already headed back to the UK to be part of BBC 5 Live's coverage of The Open, which is being played at Royal Birkdale, near Southport.

‌



Amid his hectic schedule, Chapman has also managed to squeeze in an edition of the Sports Agents podcast, which he co-hosts with Logan, who asked him: "Are you already kind of working out where you're going to watch the World Cup final? Because you're working on it, aren't you?" Chapman responded: "No, I'm not. No, I'm not." He added: "No, I'll be at the golf."

Regarding his plans for Sunday, Chapman said: "I'm doing The Open golf that weekend, and then I will drive back from The Open golf listening to Kelly and the build-up on the radio and then I'll catch some of you on the telly."

‌



Pundits turn on England boss Thomas Tuchel as change demanded after World Cup 'catastrophe' READ MORE :

Mark Chapman forced into BBC correction after Gary Lineker quip on England coverage READ MORE :

While The Open is shown on Sky Sports in the UK, 5 Live has radio rights. Meanwhile, the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain will be shown live by both the BBC and ITV.

Logan is set to front the BBC's coverage, while Mark Pougatch will anchor ITV's broadcast. One of Chapman's final contributions at the World Cup saw him share a light-hearted exchange with Richards about former BBC presenter Gary Lineker.

View 2 Images Chapman is one of the BBC's most experienced presenters (Image: Mike Hewitt, Getty Images)

‌



The ex-Match of the Day host's name came up during a broadcast, which displayed a graphic of Jude Bellingham's contributions, with Lineker appearing prominently on the list.

That prompted ex-Manchester City defender Richards, who is part of Lineker's The Rest is Football show, to make a joke at his friend's expense.

He said: "One thing I don't like on that list, another graphic that's got Gary Lineker on there. He's just text me now, he's dropping down the table, thank god for that!"

Chapman cheekily shot back: "Gary, Gary who?" Before swiftly backtracking: "Joke, joke, joke, before everyone piles on. Goodness me!"

Sports.title: Lionel Messi and Argentina players' telling reaction to Jordan Pickford's water bottle notes
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi and Argentina players' telling reaction to Jordan Pickford's water bottle notes

England's Jordan Pickford may well have left Lionel Messi and several other Argentina stars impressed with his homework for their World Cup semi-final

View 2 Images Lionel Messi was among the Argentina players that reacted to Jordan Pickford's water bottle that had penalty information (Image: Tyc Sports)

Football fans have suggested Lionel Messi and Argentina stars appeared impressed at the accuracy of their penalty-taking assessments on Jordan Pickford's water bottle. Following their 2-1 comeback win over England, several Argentina players, including Messi, were captured on camera deep in conversation huddled around looking at the goalkeeper's water bottle.

‌



A close-up image of the bottle later emerged, showing it titled with 'Argentina penalty taker list', which made it clear it was Pickford's that had been left on the pitch. Messi, as their first penalty-taker, was at the very top and next to his name it read, 'fake left - dive right'.

‌



The Argentina captain, Nico Gonzalez, Marcos Senesi and a member of staff were the first Argentina players to take notice with the former seemingly double-taking at the directions next to his name. Senesi appeared to explain exactly what it meant with Messi appearing to nod in agreement.

‌



England star interrupts Lionel Messi interview after bruising World Cup exit READ MORE :

Argentina goalscorer Enzo Fernandez was also presented with the water bottle and looked to point straight at his name before letting out a relieved smile.

He also pointed up to the skies as if he was thankful the clash did not go to penalties.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi reacts to Jordan Pickford's water bottle (Image: Tyc Sports)

‌



The Chelsea star may have fancied his chances against Pickford had spot-kicks been required having beaten him from distance in normal time.

That superb strike cancelled out Anthony Gordon's opener before substitute Lautaro Martinez grabbed the winner.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Pickford has come under fire for failing to save Fernandez's effort with Jamie Carragher, Gary Neville and even Jude Bellingham all sharing similar thoughts.

Upon watching a replay on the big screen, the latter appeared to angrily exclaim: "It's the middle of the goal!" In his column for The Telegraph, Carragher wrote: "Pickford should still have saved Enzo Fernández’s shot."

‌



Gary Neville was also critical of the Everton shot-stopper on the Stick to Football World Cup Watch Party. He said: "Not gone in the corner, that. He's got to save that, got to save it. He's past it."

Thomas Tuchel has also been slammed for his defensive changes with a significant amount of the second half still to play. Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O'Reilly were the defenders introduced, with John Stones, Gordon and Declan Rice among those that went off.

Despite their elimination, England will not depart the United States until after the weekend as they face France in a third-place play-off on Saturday.

Sports.title: England superfan's flag displayed at every Three Lions World Cup game - just weeks after he died
Sports.content:
England superfan's flag displayed at every Three Lions World Cup game - just weeks after he died

Brian Robson, 63, had followed the Three Lions for decades before he tragically died from cancer just weeks before the tournament. He had a ticket for the final in the US because he was a 'top capper', a dedicated England fans' club member

View 5 Images The image of Brian Robson in New York (Image: Garford Beck)

He was one of England's most loyal fans throughout his life - and remained with them 'in spirit' even after his death, right up to the World Cup semi-final.

‌



Brian Robson, 63, had followed the Three Lions for decades before he tragically died from cancer just weeks before the tournament. He had a ticket for the final in the US because he was a 'top capper', one of the most dedicated members of the England fans' club.

‌



He also had tickets for the World Cup finals which he attended in Russia in 2018 and Qatar in 2022, and he travelled the world following the national side. His passion took him from his hometown of Ashington in Northumberland to Serbia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, San Marino, Albania, Lithuania, Portugal, and Czechia.

‌



He became a much-loved figure with the England fans' team, helping organise games against supporters' sides from across the globe. And his own England fan club has carried his flag - and photo - to all of our games in the US.

View 5 Images Brian's flag seen in at the game in New York/New Jersey

Argentinian media mock England 'humiliation' and take aim at Jude Bellingham in World Cup loss READ MORE :

Victoria and David Beckham heartbroken as England's World Cup dream over READ MORE :

His close friend Garford Beck, 64, of London, said: "We wanted him here with us and carried his flag and photo everywhere." Mark Trigg, 52, a chef from Derby, added: "He is not forgotten."

‌



Brian's proud son Lewis, 28, of Ashington, Northumberland, said: "He was expecting to be in the US and had his ticket for the final in case England got there. He was a super fan, in the top percentile, so he received the best ticket deal.

View 5 Images Brian Robson's flag on tour

"We saw the England v France game during our holiday in Portugal at Euro 2004, when Rooney was a young player. I was seven years old. He went to Germany in 2006, attended Euro 2012, Russia in 2018, Qatar in 2022, as well as the two most recent European championships.

‌



"It hurts": England fans reflect on England's World Cup semi-final knock out in Miami

"He traveled to parts of the world which he would never normally have seen, like Serbia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Azerbijan and San Marino. He had to put in the miles to get the tickets, he saw England in the Euro final and had tickets for the World Cup finals in Russia and Qatar.

View 5 Images Brian Robson (far right) at the World Cup in Qatar (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

‌



"It is all the more remarkable given where we live: he would fly from Newcastle, sometimes via Dublin or Palma, and then take a bus or a train.

"It was not just about 90 minutes of football; what made it special for Dad were the friendships and connections he made while he was there. I would ask: 'Why are you going back there dad?' He would say: 'Because we had a great time last year'. It was about the moments outside the stadium."

View 5 Images Brian's flag in Mexico before the England game (Image: Family photo/Garford Beck)

Article continues below

Brian, a factory worker, was often spotted on TV coverage of England with his Ashington flag.

Ashington born and bred, he followed his beloved Newcastle United up and down the land, with his father Brian snr, now 90, whose family lived just two streets away from the famous Charlton brothers Jack and Sir Bobby.

"I think it's a bit of freshness in the centres," said the Wales head coach. "I thought the combination with Joe and Eddie has been excellent for us but we feel Max and Ben deserve an opportunity.

"Max I thought did really well for us in the autumn, unfortunately he got injured, and then Ben has responded really well since being left out from the England game.

"It's exciting for us. Moving things around, freshening up, there's lots of travel. And obviously it's the back end of the season so it's a good opportunity for us to try a few different combinations."

Sports.title: Norris to take 10-place Belgian GP grid penalty
Sports.content:
Lando Norris will take a 10-place grid penalty at Sunday's Belgian Grand Prix.

McLaren confirmed on Thursday that Norris' MCL40 will use a new power electronics unit at Spa-Francorchamps - which will be the fourth such element the car has been fitted with this season, one more than is permitted to be used without penalty under F1's regulations.

A fourth unit automatically triggers a 10-place grid drop for the reigning world champion from wherever he qualifies for Sunday's race. Norris will therefore start no higher than 11th.

McLaren said they are fitting the fresh unit to take advantage of battery reliability improvements from engine suppliers Mercedes after failures with initial units earlier in the season, with Spa-Francorchamps chosen as the circuit to take the penalty due to its relatively overtaking-friendly nature.

A McLaren statement read: "Car Number 1's first power electronics unit suffered a terminal issue in China, which meant Lando was unable to start the race.

"Lando's second power electronics unit, fitted in Japan, needed to be withdrawn for remedial work after suffering issues in Free Practice, which necessitated moving to a third and final power electronics unit within the permitted allocation. While the second power electronics unit was able to be repaired after the Japanese Grand Prix, it suffered a terminal issue in FP2 in Monaco, and was withdrawn from our allocation once again.

Image: Norris' car suffered early-season Mercedes battery problems in China, Japan and Monaco

"While the power electronics unit we installed in Japan, and have used in every session since Miami, has worked reliably, Mercedes-AMG High Performance Powertrains has since introduced a series of reliability fixes to their new power electronics systems.

"However, in order to take advantage of these improvements, we must incur a 10-place grid penalty on Lando's car in order to take a new unit.

"We have chosen to do this in Belgium, a circuit where overtaking is relatively more prevalent, as opposed to the following two events in Hungary and Zandvoort. We now plan to use this fourth power electronics unit for the remainder of the season, in order to maximise reliability while minimising sporting penalties on Lando."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McLaren driver Lando Norris said McLaren needed to play catch-up after he qualified in P6 ahead of the British Grand Prix.

Norris, who counts Spa as a second home race as his mother is Belgian, has endured a challenging world title defence so far in the 2026 season with McLaren unable to challenge front-runners Mercedes and Ferrari on a consistent basis.

He is fifth in the Drivers' Championship after nine rounds, 82 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli. His average qualifying result is fifth place.

Mercedes have recently introduced reliability improvements for their power unit, which their title-leading works team first used two races ago in Austria and then customers Alpine and Williams last time out at Silverstone.

McLaren had not yet run Mercedes' new-specification internal combustion engines as their failure to take the race start with both cars at March's Chinese Grand Prix meant they had not reached the required mileage limits on the existing units. However, Norris and Oscar Piastri are set to take the fresh ICEs, without any penalty as they remain within the allocation, this weekend.

Sports.title: Goalkeeper Gordon, 43, retires after 25-year career
Sports.content:
Craig Gordon has retired from playing football at the age of 43.

The goalkeeper made his professional debut in 2001 and went on to play over 760 times for Hearts, Celtic, Sunderland, Cowdenbeath and Scotland.

His first of 84 international caps came in 2004, while his Scottish Cup win with Hearts in the 2005/06 season was the first of his 15 major honours.

Image: Craig Gordon helped Hearts beat Gretna in the 2005/06 Scottish Cup final

Gordon earned a spot in the Scottish FA's international roll of honour, plus at the age of 24 was inducted into Hearts' hall of fame in 2007 - the youngest player to receive such an accolade.

His £9m move to Sunderland later that year was the-then-British-record transfer fee for a goalkeeper, and in 2010 his save against Bolton was named the best save in Premier League history.

Image: Gordon joined Sunderland in 2007 for £9m

Gordon's 25-year playing career was also hampered by major injuries. A succession of ankle problems, broken arms and knee surgery saw his time at Sunderland eventually end, and a period of rehab begin.

He was then out of action for around two years and took up coaching as he battled against a career-threatening condition from 2012.

From being unable to walk pain-free, Gordon recovered and signed for Celtic, where he won six Premiership titles, five League Cups and three Scottish Cups.

Image: Gordon won six league titles when at Celtic

Following the expiry of his contract at Celtic Park, Gordon returned to Hearts, where he continued to impress before another setback. A double leg break on Christmas Eve 2022 that left his career in doubt again.

However, after more surgery, Gordon recovered again and returned to action for Hearts and Scotland.

Image: Gordon broke his leg in two places when playing for Hearts in 2022

He played his part in last season's title bid as Hearts missed out on the final day of the Premiership season, plus was in the Scotland squad for the World Cup at 43.

Following 25 years of success, individual honours and perseverance, the goalkeeper has called time on his remarkable career.

"I'm not much of a singer, but I improved a little after 84 renditions of the national anthem. The biggest names, at the biggest stadiums, on the biggest stages - I've savoured every moment of it.

"Now the gloves are finally off and I bid farewell to my playing career. You, the fans, have given me everything, and it has been a privilege to represent you.

"I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have. From the bottom of my heart, thank you."

Sports.title: How hard is it for Littler to go back to back at the World Matchplay?
Sports.content:
The World Matchplay was a tournament dominated by Phil Taylor as - from 1994 to 2014 - he picked up 15 wins in Blackpool out of a possible 21. Yes, you read that correctly.

Taylor had control of the Winter Gardens for nearly two decades, making going back to back look like light work.

He bossed the Blackpool stage and it appeared as if defending the title at such a tournament was a simple ask. He dominated so much that, after he retired, the trophy was named after him.

Then, along came Michael van Gerwen who continued the trend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Phil Taylor wins his 16th and last World Matchplay title

The Dutchman secured Matchplay supremacy in 2015 and 2016, beating James Wade then Taylor himself to make it a double at the seaside.

MVG's accolades heading into both of those tournaments made incredible reading.

Going into the 2015 Matchplay he held the World Grand Prix, European Championship, Masters and UK Open crowns.

Then, going into the 2016 Matchplay, he possessed the World Matchplay, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts, Players Championship Finals, Masters, UK Open and Premier League titles.

He was also world No 1 on both occasions and won a ridiculous 11 Euro Tour events out of 18 across 2015 and 2016.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael van Gerwen hits a nine-darter at the 2012 World Matchplay

While Matchplay dominance had looked a certainty, it was a trend that was then quickly bucked because Van Gerwen only managed it once despite his dominance during the late 2010s and Luke Humphries failed at the first hurdle, a smattering of winners coming in the interlude between two players on top.

The current champion is world No 1 Luke Littler who also boasts the World Grand Prix, Grand Slam of Darts, Players Championship Finals, World Championship, World Masters, UK Open, Premier League and World Cup titles.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look back at some other shocking exits that have happened in Blackpool

Similarly to Littler, Van Gerwen was untouchable as the best player in the world. His one downfall? He did not win the World Darts Championship on either occasion in 2015 or 2016 before triumphing again in 2017.

Littler has won the last two World Championships and is now looking to become the first player in a decade to retain the Matchplay title and tick off another bit of history.

How the Matchplay goes literally decides the trajectory of Littler's year. If he retains, he continues his aim of a clean sweep. He fails? Then how many tournaments he enters for the remainder of 2026 radically changes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler hits a nine-darter at the 2025 World Matchplay

Littler did what Van Gerwen did not when he claimed World Darts Championship wins two years in a row.

"If I could choose, I would swap all the other tournaments I won for this one. It's the most important one and I'm going to try and get my title back, but the standard is so high you're not allowed to make any mistakes," Van Gerwen said in November 2015 ahead of the Worlds.

Littler does not have to swap any silverware for the Sid Waddell Trophy as he retained the crown.

It is now time to show he can do it again on the Matchplay stage too.

Will a win at the Matchplay bring a title defence in Minehead?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Michael Bridge and Paul Nicholson discuss Luke Littler's 2026 season

Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge...

"He will be on the ball, no doubt about it. He hasn't played much lately, he's obviously been in America for the World Series, he's been doing a lot of PR events, but we know he's not being part of the EuroTour at the moment.

"There are still question marks whether he'll do any Pro Tours at all. I think he might change his mind if he wins the Matchplay because he will want to win everything.

"I know people in his team are denying that, but I think he will go for it if he wins the Matchplay.

"We know Luke, we know that when there is a goal, he is so incredibly driven.

"There has been a suggestion to me that it's too late for him to get to Minehead, but there is definitely time. There is plenty of time.

"But if he does win this, then I think it could propel him to maybe go to Minehead."

When is the World Matchplay live on Sky Sports?

The World Matchplay commences on Saturday July 18 and ends on Sunday July 26.

All nine days of the event will be shown live on Sky Sports, with coverage of the opening day commencing on Sky Sports+ at 7pm Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW

Sports.title: Forget tactics, which England players failed to step up when needed most?
Sports.content:
England's World Cup journey came to a rather dramatic end against Argentina and their exit has led to one very simple question: why?

A lot of the blame has gone towards the decision to retreat after Anthony Gordon's goal just before the hour mark. The switch to the back five invited pressure, and Thomas Tuchel's side simply couldn't hold on.

However, the one thing the England boss has maintained throughout the tournament is that there can be no doubting the players' mentality. The game in Atlanta seemed to bring that into question.

England were already defending before the change in formation. Players were succumbing to the environment they were in. Not all, but some. Who managed to find another gear when their country needed them most? And who failed to deliver in a game of such magnitude?
